headline: Metal prices lift margins, but profit dips sequentially
summary_short: Century Aluminum reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $752.1M, up 15.8% q/q, while gross profit rose 91.8% q/q to $227.9M on higher aluminum prices.
summary_long: Revenue rose 15.8% q/q to $752.1M as higher LME and regional aluminum premiums added $80.5M and favorable volume/mix from the Mt. Holly and Grundartangi restarts added $34.4M, partly offset by lower third-party alumina sales. Gross profit jumped 91.8% q/q to $227.9M on the same price gains plus $34.3M of favorable power-price realization, though operating income fell 43.4% q/q to $211.6M because Q1 2026 included a one-time $287.9M gain on the Hawesville sale that Q2 lacked. Net income of $249.3M (EPS $2.52) fell 26.1% q/q for the same reason, but swung to a profit from a year-ago loss. Cash rose 40.7% q/q to $343.4M on Hawesville sale proceeds and Grundartangi insurance recoveries. Century guided FY2026 capex to $180-190M.
confidence_notes: Q1 2026 operating and net income included a one-time $287.9M pre-tax gain on the February 2026 Hawesville sale; the reported q/q declines in operating income and EPS are a comparability artifact of that gain rolling off, not a deterioration in underlying metal-price economics. The 10-Q also references an immaterial Jamalco consolidation-method restatement of prior-period comparatives (no impact on reported net income).

drivers.explanation: Higher LME and regional aluminum premiums added $80.5M and favorable volume/mix from the Mt. Holly and Grundartangi restarts added $34.4M, partly offset by lower alumina sales.
Metal-price gains plus $34.3M of favorable power-price realization from improved U.S. weather drove the sequential increase.
Q1 2026 included a one-time $287.9M gain on the Hawesville sale that did not recur in Q2, more than offsetting the gross-profit gain.
Fell for the same reason as operating income — the absence of Q1's one-time Hawesville sale gain — despite stronger underlying metal-price margins.
Cash rose on proceeds from the Hawesville sale and Grundartangi insurance recoveries related to the 2025 transformer failure.
Underlying aluminum-price and restart-driven profitability improved sequentially; reported profit looks lower only because Q1 carried a one-time asset-sale gain.
